correctness.rationale: For each order n=7,8,9 and every length L=1..10,14,20, enumerate.cpp visits every integer x in [0,2^L), and tests exact Hamming-radius-two coverage using OR of all length-n window balls; crosscheck.cpp independently tests every target directly using bitwise Hamming distances. The two programs reproduced 44 exact count rows, with no covers below L=10,14,20, counts 110,28,20 at those lengths, and 11,2,1 rotation classes of full size L. Source-level predicates are equivalent to the mathematical definition, so full finite enumeration proves the claim; logs are accompanied by sources, full census, and orbit list.

value.rationale: The number of nonequivalent shortest covering cycles is the natural equality-case invariant of an extremal covering-sequence problem. Earlier tables establish how short a sequence can be, but not whether there are alternative optimal designs. At order nine the new upper bound 20 equals the generic lower bound of 20 indexed rotations, hence establishes rigidity/uniqueness. Across consecutive orders the complete classification 11->2->1 is a substantial natural finite cutoff and supplies reproducible benchmarks for covering-sequence constructions; the result is not an arbitrary partial table.
